newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-HUSTON, HEINEN SHARE LEAD AT TEXAS OPEN AFTER FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HUSTON, HEINEN SHARE LEAD AT TEXAS OPEN AFTER FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Long-hitting John Huston eagled two of the first five holes on his way to a share of the first-round lead with Mike Heinen at the $1.2 million LaCantena Texas Open on Thursday.
"I really hadn't made a putt and I was four under," said Huston, who shot a six-under-par 66 in delightful conditions at hilly LaCantena.
Huston and Heinen were one stroke ahead of Hugh Royer and South African David Frost, while new superstar Tiger Woods was three shots back, tied for 10th at three-under 69.
Four players failed to complete the first round due to darkness, but none was near the lead.
Huston's first eagle came at the par-four second, where he holed a four-iron from 206 yards. At the par-five fifth, he bladed home a sand wedge from 30 feet.
"I drove the ball well," continued Huston. "I think that's going to be the key for the week, keep it out of the rough."
Huston, 35th on the PGA Tour money list, has not been satisfied with his year: "It's been very frustrating. As well as I've putted, I haven't done very well.
"I've struggled off the tee. That's trickled down to the rest of my game. I've tried just about everything."
Heinen, meanwhile, will lose his tour card unless he wins about $70,000 in the next two weeks.
"I had a bad time early in the year," said Heinen, whose lone tour victory was at New Orleans in 1994.
"Lately I've been hitting the ball really well. I'm starting to gain confidence back with my ball striking. I want to win one of the next two tournaments, and make a horrible year a pretty good one."
Woods, followed by an enormous gallery, mixed seven birdies with four bogeys.
"I'm pretty happy with the way I started," said the three-time U.S. amateur champion, who won last week's Las Vegas Invitational in only his fifth start as a professional.
